title: Culture, markets and etiquette
text: For markets, compare prices respectfully and buy crafts from sellers who can explain provenance. At temples, dargahs and ghats, follow dress guidance, remove shoes when requested and seek permission before photography.

title: Textile and block-print traditions
text: Textiles and block printing vary by region, workshop and technique. Ask artisans about process, materials, natural or synthetic dyes, care and provenance. Seek permission before photographing people or work in progress; buy only with clear price and receipt.

title: Jaipur blue pottery
text: Blue pottery is a recognized Jaipur craft tradition. Workshops and products vary; ask about maker, materials, food-safe use, care and breakage/shipping. Do not assume a shop item is handmade or locally produced without asking.

title: Nathdwara Pichwai painting
text: Nathdwara is associated with Pichwai painting and devotional imagery. Visit working artists respectfully, ask about permission and provenance, and consider the religious context of the artwork. Prices, authenticity and workshop access vary.

title: Miniature painting traditions
text: Rajasthan has multiple miniature-painting traditions and regional styles. Ask the artist about school/style, materials, time invested and provenance. Avoid treating a broad “Rajasthani miniature” label as proof of origin.

title: Folk performance etiquette
text: Ghoomar and other folk performances may be staged for visitors or presented in community/festival contexts. Check whether photography is permitted, respect performers and avoid intrusive flash or blocking the audience. Confirm event timing directly.

title: Kalbelia and performer respect
text: Kalbelia is a living performance tradition. Engage with performers respectfully, clarify payment and photography terms, and avoid stereotypes or non-consensual filming. Show schedules and availability vary by venue and season.

title: Fair and festival etiquette
text: Before attending a fair, confirm dates, venue, transport and crowd arrangements with official organizers. Respect sacred areas, ask before photographing people and animals, and plan water, meeting points and an exit route. Dates and programming can change.

title: Ghats and sacred water etiquette
text: At Pushkar ghats, follow posted and locally explained customs, dress modestly, keep footwear and photography within site rules, and do not pressure people for photos. Decline unsolicited paid rituals politely and clarify any voluntary offering before participating.

title: Dargah visit etiquette
text: At Ajmer Sharif, follow current entry, dress, footwear and security instructions from the shrine authorities. Keep quiet in worship areas and ask before photographing people or rituals. Be cautious of unsolicited offers and clarify any donation or service before agreeing.

title: Community-led cultural visits
text: In tribal regions, arrange visits through hosts who welcome visitors and explain expectations. Ask consent before entering homes, photographing people or discussing cultural practices. Pay fairly for agreed services and do not publish sensitive information without permission.

title: Animal-related tourism
text: Before any camel, horse or other animal activity, assess welfare, working conditions, water, shade, rest and operator conduct. Decline activities involving distress, coercion or unsafe handling. Availability and licensing should be verified locally.
